8.testability_note: Verifying data loss on container restart or OOM kill requires platform-level control (restart server process). The harness cannot trigger server restarts or observe post-crash state.

9.testability_note: This is a forward-looking platform compatibility concern for a hypothetical future change (migrating away from in-memory storage). There is nothing to test currently via the HTTP harness.

10.testability_note: Directly testable: POST a note to get its ID, then issue PUT or DELETE with that ID and verify the operations succeed without any auth token. The harness supports PUT and DELETE with note ID path param.

11.testability_note: The API-level aspect is testable: POST a note for postcode A, then GET notes for postcode B and assert postcode B returns its own notes. The UI wiring aspect (silent failure) cannot be verified via the API harness.

12.testability_note: Substantially overlaps idea_index 3 and 8. Requires server restart capability which the harness lacks. Not testable via HTTP calls alone.

13.testability_note: Directly testable: POST a note with content > 500 chars directly via the harness (bypassing UI). This is essentially the same test as idea_index 4 — the time-framing angle doesn't change testability.

14.testability_note: Substantially overlaps idea_index 6. All four HTTP methods are exercisable by the harness. Smoke-testing each endpoint for a valid response is straightforward.

15.testability_note: The wiring between PostcodeInfoPanel, PostcodeNotes, and useNotes hook is a UI/component integration concern. The API harness cannot render components or test React hook wiring — this requires a component test or E2E setup.

16.testability_note: Duplicate of ideas 3, 8, 12. Server restart is required to verify; harness cannot control server lifecycle.

17.testability_note: Concurrency simulation (parallel requests) is outside the harness's capability. Sequential ordering can be tested (see idea 5/32), but concurrent interleaving cannot be replicated.

18.testability_note: This is a UI keyboard interaction test (Escape key in edit textarea). The harness only calls HTTP endpoints — it cannot simulate keyboard events or inspect DOM state.

19.testability_note: Concerns UI state transitions (edit textarea dismissal after save/cancel). The harness cannot render the UI or observe component state — requires E2E or component-level testing.

20.testability_note: Visual/aesthetic verification (styling, layout, alignment) cannot be performed via the HTTP API harness. Requires visual regression tooling or E2E screenshot comparison.

21.testability_note: The claim is about the content/quality of error messages rendered in the UI. The harness can confirm the API returns an error status, but cannot inspect what the UI renders to the user.

22.testability_note: Directly testable: POST a note to get its ID, then issue PUT/DELETE with that ID (no auth) and assert the server permits it. This documents the current permissive behaviour as found in KI-2026-011. Harness supports PUT/DELETE with note ID.

23.testability_note: CORS testing requires sending requests with custom Origin headers from a disallowed origin and inspecting Access-Control-Allow-Origin response headers. The harness cannot send custom headers.

24.testability_note: Partially testable: POST a large number of notes for a postcode and observe whether the server imposes any limit (e.g., 429, 400) or silently accepts all. The harness supports repeated POST calls. OOM crash itself requires monitoring beyond the harness.

25.testability_note: Concurrent request simulation is outside the harness's capability. The ordering test angle is covered by idea 5/32 sequentially, but true concurrency cannot be replicated with this harness.

26.testability_note: Substantially overlaps idea 24. Partially testable by flooding the server with POST requests and checking for cap enforcement. Actual OOM detection is outside harness capability.

27.testability_note: Directly testable: POST a note (session A equivalent), capture the note ID, then issue PUT/DELETE with that ID without any session token (session B equivalent). Harness supports all required methods. Overlaps heavily with idea 10/22.

28.testability_note: p95 latency measurement requires load generation and percentile analysis tooling (e.g., k6, wrk). The harness can make single requests and observe response time, but cannot measure p95 across a distribution.

29.testability_note: Sequential ordering is testable: POST notes A, B, C and verify GET returns them in that order. True concurrent ordering non-determinism cannot be simulated, but the sequential invariant is a meaningful baseline check.

30.testability_note: This is an architectural/code-quality claim about the absence of a storage abstraction. Not testable via HTTP calls — verifying the architecture requires code inspection, not API interaction.

31.testability_note: This is a claim about test-suite reliability and CI gating, not API behaviour. Monitoring fail rate trends requires CI pipeline observation across multiple runs — not achievable via the HTTP harness.

32.testability_note: Directly testable: POST notes A, B, C sequentially for a postcode, then GET and assert the array order matches A, B, C. The harness supports sequential POST and GET with postalCode.

33.testability_note: Directly testable: POST a note for postcode A, GET notes for postcode B, and assert the response does not contain the note created for A. Harness fully supports this with postalCode path param.

34.testability_note: Directly testable: issue a PUT request with a non-existent note ID and assert the response is 404. The harness supports PUT with a note ID path parameter.

35.testability_note: Partially testable: POST a large volume of notes without deleting them and verify the server either enforces a cap or accepts all (documenting the absence of a cap). Full OOM detection requires server monitoring beyond the harness.

36.testability_note: Directly testable: POST a note with specific content, then GET the notes list and assert the content field matches exactly. The harness supports POST with content body and GET with postalCode.

37.testability_note: This concerns the UI 'Add Note' button's enabled/disabled state in response to textarea content. The harness only calls the API and cannot inspect or manipulate DOM button states.

38.testability_note: Largely a duplicate of ideas 3/8/12/16 reframed as a user experience story. Server restart capability is required; harness cannot control server lifecycle or observe user-facing consequences.

39.testability_note: The claim is about the content and actionability of user-facing error messages rendered in the UI when the API is unavailable. The harness cannot simulate API unavailability from the client's perspective or inspect rendered UI text.

40.testability_note: This is a process/tracking claim about promoting a test from At-Risk to Flaky status. It describes a CI monitoring action, not an API behaviour that can be exercised via HTTP calls.

41.testability_note: This is a longitudinal CI analytics/monitoring recommendation, not a discrete API behaviour. The harness cannot accumulate fail-rate statistics across PRs or make quarantine decisions.

0.testability_note: This is a structural/coverage audit claim about code artifacts, not a behaviour that can be probed via HTTP. The harness cannot inspect what test files exist or measure service-layer coverage independently.

1.testability_note: This is a documentation/structure observation about which Gherkin feature file contains notes scenarios. The HTTP harness cannot verify file organisation or spec traceability.

2.testability_note: Fully testable now: POST a note to postcode '00180', then GET /api/notes/00100 and assert the note does not appear. All steps use plain HTTP with postalCode and content body fields.

3.testability_note: Verifying data loss after server restart requires controlling server lifecycle (stop/start), which the HTTP harness cannot do. The claim is real but untestable with current tooling.

4.testability_note: Directly testable: POST a note with content exceeding 500 characters and assert it is either rejected (4xx) or stored as-is (revealing the bypass). The harness supports POST with a content body of arbitrary length.

5.testability_note: Partially testable: POST multiple notes sequentially to a postcode and then GET the list, asserting response order matches insertion order. Concurrent race condition itself requires parallel request control the harness lacks.

6.testability_note: Each endpoint (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE) can be probed individually with the harness to confirm they return non-404/405 responses and behave as expected.

7.testability_note: UI control rendering (textarea placeholder, character counter, button labels) requires a browser/DOM environment. The harness only calls the API and cannot inspect rendered HTML or UI elements.

8.testability_note: Verifying data loss after platform restart requires controlling container/process lifecycle. The HTTP harness cannot trigger or detect server restarts.

9.testability_note: A forward-looking platform compatibility concern about Alpine musl libc. Not testable via HTTP; requires a future storage migration that hasn't happened yet.

10.testability_note: Directly testable: POST a note, capture its ID, then send a PUT or DELETE using that ID and assert the operation succeeds without any auth check. The harness supports DELETE and PUT with note id path params.

11.testability_note: Partially testable at the API layer: POST a note to postcode A, then GET notes for postcode B, and assert postcode B returns its own notes (not A's). The UI/hook wiring aspect (KI-2026-008) requires a UI test harness.

12.testability_note: Essentially a duplicate of idea_index 3 and 8 from a Time heuristic angle. Confirming data loss requires server restart control that the harness does not have.

13.testability_note: Testable now: POST a note with content > 500 characters via the API (bypassing UI). Assert whether server accepts or rejects. Covers the same ground as idea 4 from a different framing — one test covers both.

14.testability_note: All four HTTP methods can be exercised directly. Substantively overlaps idea 6 but framed as a capability completeness check rather than interface check — one suite of tests covers both.

15.testability_note: The wiring between PostcodeInfoPanel, PostcodeNotes, and useNotes hook is a UI integration concern. The HTTP harness can only verify the API itself, not whether the component renders or wires correctly.

16.testability_note: Near-duplicate of ideas 3, 8, 12. Server restart control is required and unavailable in the harness.

17.testability_note: The concurrent/non-deterministic ordering claim requires parallel request execution and concurrency control that the harness cannot perform. Sequential ordering is testable but not the concurrency angle.

18.testability_note: Escape-key keyboard behaviour is a UI interaction that requires browser/DOM simulation. The HTTP harness cannot send keyboard events or test UI component state.

19.testability_note: Edit-mode dismissal (showing/hiding the textarea after save/cancel) is a UI rendering concern that requires a browser/component test harness, not an HTTP API call.

20.testability_note: Visual/layout aesthetics require visual regression tooling or manual inspection. Not testable via the HTTP API harness.

21.testability_note: Error message content and formatting is rendered in the UI component, not returned as a user-visible string by the API. The harness can confirm an error response code but not the human-facing error message text.

22.testability_note: Directly testable: POST a note, record the returned ID, then PUT/DELETE that ID without any session token and assert the operation succeeds — confirming missing ownership enforcement. Fully within harness capability.

23.testability_note: CORS enforcement requires sending requests with an Origin header from a disallowed domain and inspecting Access-Control response headers. The harness cannot send custom headers.

24.testability_note: Partially testable: POST a very large number of notes to a postcode and observe whether the server remains responsive, returns errors, or slows down. A full OOM crash test requires load tooling, but basic unbounded-growth can be probed with repeated POSTs.

25.testability_note: Concurrency and parallel runner state sharing cannot be reproduced by the HTTP harness, which is single-threaded and sequential by design.

26.testability_note: Near-duplicate of idea 24. Partially testable via sustained POST requests to observe lack of enforcement. Full OOM testing requires load tooling beyond the harness.

27.testability_note: Directly testable: create a note in one logical session (POST), then PUT/DELETE the returned note ID without any session scoping. The harness supports this fully. Substantively overlaps ideas 10 and 22.

28.testability_note: p95 latency measurement requires load generation and percentile-level timing instrumentation. The HTTP harness can measure single-request response time but not p95 under load.

29.testability_note: Concurrent-request non-determinism cannot be reproduced by the sequential HTTP harness. Sequential insertion-order is testable (covered by idea 32) but the concurrent variant is not.

30.testability_note: Architectural / maintainability debt observation. No HTTP-level test can verify the absence of a storage abstraction or persistence interface. Requires code inspection.

31.testability_note: Test suite flakiness due to parallel runner state sharing is a meta-testing concern, not an API behaviour. Cannot be demonstrated via the HTTP harness.

32.testability_note: Directly testable: POST two notes with distinct content in sequence, then GET the list and assert the order matches insertion order. The harness supports sequential POST and GET.

33.testability_note: Directly testable: POST a note to postcode '00180', then GET /api/notes/00100 and assert the note is absent. Substantively the same test as idea 2 — one test covers both claims.

34.testability_note: Directly testable: PUT to /api/notes/<nonexistent-id> and assert the response is 404. The harness supports PUT with a note id path parameter.

35.testability_note: Partially testable: POST a large volume of notes in a loop and observe server behaviour. Full OOM crash testing requires load tooling; confirming no count limit is achievable. Overlaps ideas 24/26.

36.testability_note: Directly testable: POST a note with specific content, then GET the list for the same postcode and assert the submitted content appears in the response. Core CRUD consistency check, fully within harness capability.

37.testability_note: Button enabled/disabled state is a UI-layer concern driven by textarea value. The HTTP harness cannot inspect DOM state or interact with UI controls.

38.testability_note: User experience after server restart (data loss perception) is a qualitative/UX concern and a platform lifecycle scenario. Neither is testable via the HTTP harness.

39.testability_note: Error message content/actionability is rendered in the UI component; the HTTP API returns a status code and possibly a JSON error body, but the human-readable user-facing message requires UI inspection.

40.testability_note: This is a test health register process/governance claim about promoting a status label. Not a functional API behaviour testable via HTTP.

41.testability_note: A longitudinal trend-monitoring claim about cumulative test failure rates across future PRs. This is a QE process concern, not an HTTP-testable functional behaviour.
